channel.title: What NBA players and coaches have said about Martin Luther King | HoopsMatic
channel.description: The latest quotes about Martin Luther King from NBA players, coaches and executives, with context and sources.

item.title: Kenny Smith on Martin Luther King, Bill Russell
item.description:
Kenny Smith:

“Bill Russell was my first coach. Bill Russell, he had a rule, I had to sit next to him on every plane ride and every bus ride as a rookie. He would talk and he'd say stuff like, 'Yeah, Kenny, back in our day, I was with, me and Malcolm X would go over here and we go eat.'I'm like, 'Malcolm X?' He's like, 'Yeah, Malcolm X.' He would like, 'Yeah, Martin Luther King Jr.' He would tell me stories about them like they were so casual. The people who made me, like him.”

Kenny Smith on Martin Luther King, Bill Russell, May 27, 2026. Source: YouTube.

item.title: Donald Trump on Kobe Bryant, Tiger Woods, Martin Luther King, Muhammad Ali
item.description:
This was where he mentioned Bryant as one of the national figures.

“Martin Luther King Jr., Muhammad Ali. Not a bad athlete, what do you think, Muhammad, not too bad, and the late Kobe Bryant. People love Kobe Bryant. We're going to save Tiger Woods for another time,”

Donald Trump on Kobe Bryant, Tiger Woods, Martin Luther King, Muhammad Ali, Feb 20, 2025. Source: Clutch Points.

item.title: Walt Frazier on Martin Luther King, Jackie Robinson
item.description:
Tommy Beer:Fantastic, poignant quote just now from Clyde Frazier on MLK:

“I think Jackie Robinson put us on the field, but Martin Luther King put us behind the mic, put us in the front office. Made other people look at us from a different perspective.”

Walt Frazier on Martin Luther King, Jackie Robinson, Jan 15, 2024. Source: Twitter @TommyBeer.

item.title: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar on Martin Luther King
item.description:
“We are supposed to be the land of the free and the home of the brave. Dr. King wanted America to be held up, accountable to that aspiration.”

Kareem Abdul-Jabbar on Martin Luther King, Jan 18, 2021. Source: Sports Illustrated.

item.title: Monty Williams on Martin Luther King
item.description:
“Because of that, you heard the family members talk about Dr. King and many others who were not just speaking out, but sacrificing a ton so that our world, our country could be a better place.”

Monty Williams on Martin Luther King, Jan 18, 2021. Source: USA Today Sports.

item.title: Monty Williams on Martin Luther King
item.description:
Gina Mizell:Monty on playing in Memphis on MLK Day:

“What a blessing and an honor... I just hope that it doesn’t just become something we do. I hope it continues to become a season in the year where we really think about what Dr. King sacrificed so that a guy like me could be in this position”

Monty Williams on Martin Luther King, Jan 18, 2021. Source: Twitter @ginamizell.

item.title: Terry Stotts on Martin Luther King
item.description:
Stotts told The Athletic in a phone interview.

“It’s really important for our history. The way I look at it, some of it is very difficult to get a hold of. Some of the things that were done in our history are not things to be proud of. Kind of an ugly truth at times — but also, the way that African Americans have overcome some of the hurdles that they’ve faced in the history of our country. What Martin Luther King and many others were able to do is something that everyone should know about and everyone should admire.”

Terry Stotts on Martin Luther King, Feb 15, 2020. Source: The Athletic.

item.title: Thurl Bailey on Martin Luther King
item.description:
Still, Bailey would feel King’s impact.

“Over the years, they helped me learn more about who Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was,”

Thurl Bailey on Martin Luther King, Jan 21, 2019. Source: NBA.com.

item.title: Austin Rivers on Martin Luther King
item.description:
Austin Rivers:

“My parents had to go through much worse dating in the era they did — a white woman dating a black guy when my mom was in college. We had people in the KKK come burn our house down in San Antonio. I don’t like to talk about this. I was 4 years old. I remember what the house looked like. I remember my mom … There’s been a lot of things happen to my family, a lot of things happen to my mom and dad, specifically. It means a lot more than people think it means. I don’t just have Martin Luther King on my leg for no reason.”

Austin Rivers on Martin Luther King, Jan 20, 2019. Source: Houston Chronicle.

item.title: Gregg Popovich on Martin Luther King
item.description:
Tom Orsborn:Pop on MLK Day and Dr. King's legacy:

“Just about everything he said was right on the money, from the heart & true. Today you don’t even know what is true & what is false. It’s another day to hope that reasonable people can come back to understanding a better path for everybody.”

Gregg Popovich on Martin Luther King, Jan 20, 2019. Source: Twitter @tom_orsborn.

item.title: Jason Wexler on Martin Luther King
item.description:
“FedEx Forum, to me, is the greatest address in sports. Our address is 191 Beale Street, and our boundaries are Beale Street (where the blues took hold as an iconic American music institution), B.B. King Boulevard, Martin Luther King Avenue and Church park, named for Robert Church, who was the first African-American millionaire, post-Civil War. And across the street from us is Clayborn Temple.”

Jason Wexler on Martin Luther King, Jan 15, 2018. Source: NBA.com.

item.title: Michael Malone on Martin Luther King
item.description:
“In today’s day and age, with everything we’re going through in communities across the country, (King’s) message is probably more prevalent and profound today and just as strong as it was back in the 1960swhen the civil rights movement was in its heyday,”

Michael Malone on Martin Luther King, Jan 15, 2018. Source: Denver Post.

item.title: Patty Mills on Martin Luther King
item.description:

Patty Mills on Martin Luther King, Jan 20, 2015. Source: FOXSports.com.
